title: Talent benchmarking and skill supply mapping framework
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines the Talent Benchmarking and Skill Supply Mapping (TBSSM) framework used by People Ops and hiring managers to: 1) quantify the current capability base across engineering and product teams, 2) benchmark role-level expectations against market signals, and 3) produce a prioritized skill supply plan (hire vs. upskill vs. contractor) for the next two quarters. TBSSM is intended to standardize evidence, cadence, and decision-making so hiring and development dollars are targeted where they produce measurable impact.

Objectives

- Create a single source of truth for role-level capabilities and supply gaps.
- Provide an evidence-backed prioritization for hiring vs training vs redeployment.
- Reduce time-to-fill for high-priority gaps by 20% within two quarters.
- Improve first-90-day effectiveness for new hires by aligning onboarding to benchmarked competency targets.

Scope

- Teams in scope: Engineering, Product, Applied ML, SRE, DevRel for the initial pilot (Q1–Q2 2028).
- Roles: IC and manager levels up to L6 / Sr Manager. Leadership and exec-level role profiling will follow a different cadence.
- Outputs: Quarterly skill supply map, prioritized resourcing plan (hire/upskill/contractor), and one-page role benchmark for each role family.

Key definitions

- Role benchmark: Articulated target proficiencies across 8 canonical competencies for a role (see Competency Matrix).
- Supply map: A snapshot of headcount, demonstrated proficiency, and time-to-competency (T2C) per role family.
- Gap closure plan: The set of actions (hire/upskill/contractor/internal mobility) with owners and timeline.

Ownership and governance

- Program owner: People Ops (lead: Asha Patel).
- Quarterly review owner: Workforce Planning (Diego Ramirez) + Hiring Velocity Squad.
- Role-family stewards: Hiring manager(s) for each team (primary) and Discipline Lead (secondary).
- Executive sponsor (pilot): VP People (Maya Chen).

Inputs and data sources

- HRIS: Workday — canonical headcount and tenure.
- People Data Warehouse (PDW) — aggregated training completions, performance evidence tags, and skills survey responses.
- ATS: Greenhouse — active reqs, funnel metrics, time-to-offer.
- Manager evidence packets — new-hire 30/60/90 notes, probationals, and internal transfer reviews.
- Market signals — compiled biquarterly by Recruiting (benchmarks: salary ranges, required skills from job market, and supply scarcity index).

Process (quarterly cadence)

1. Role-family inventory (week 1–2):
   - People Ops triggers a refresh job that extracts current headcount, active requisitions, and last competency assessment timestamp from PDW.
   - Output: Raw CSV — [role_family, role_level, headcount, active_reqs, last_assessed_date].

2. Evidence gathering (week 2–3):
   - Role-family steward collects manager evidence packets for all incumbents in-scope.
   - Managers submit a short skills self-assessment for each direct report using the standardized survey (10–15 min).

3. Benchmark generation (week 3–4):
   - People Ops combines internal evidence with market signals to produce a Role Benchmark (one page).
   - Role Benchmark includes target proficiency per competency, salary midpoints, and expected T2C for external hires.

4. Supply mapping and gap analysis (week 4–5):
   - PDW produces a Skill Supply Map: for each role family, compute % of incumbents at or above target proficiency, projected attrition (next 6 months), and backlog of requisitions.

5. Prioritization and resourcing plan (week 5–6):
   - Hiring Velocity Squad convenes a 60-minute prioritization review with role-family stewards and Finance rep.
   - Action outcomes: Approve hiring reqs, approve training plans, or reassign internal candidates.

6. Publish and track (week 6):
   - People Ops publishes the quarter's Skill Supply Map and Gap Closure Plan to the People Ops workspace and notifies stakeholders.

Competency Matrix (canonical competencies)

| Competency | Level 1 (Foundational) | Level 3 (Proficient) | Level 5 (Expert) |
|------------|-------------------------|----------------------|------------------|
| Systems Thinking | Understands basic service boundaries | Designs moderately complex systems with tradeoffs | Architect-level design with system-wide impact |
| Product Judgment | Follows product specs and tickets | Shapes feature scope and tradeoffs | Defines multi-quarter product strategy |
| Code Quality & Ownership | Contributes with reviews | Owns services end-to-end | Mentors across teams, drives standards |
| Reliability & Ops | Can use runbooks | Sets SLOs and incident playbooks | Leads reliability strategy across platform |
| ML & Data Literacy (if applicable) | Interprets simple metrics | Evaluates model outputs and drift | Sets model governance & evals |
| Collaboration & Communication | Communicates within team | Influences cross-functional partners | Coaches leaders on communication strategy |
| Leadership (for manager tracks) | Manages small projects | Leads team-level outcomes | Scales org capability and talent |
| Learning Agility | Completes assigned training | Applies new skills in projects | Systematically spreads learning practices |

(Each competency row is scored on a 1–5 rubric in the operating spreadsheet.)

Templates and artifact checklist

- Role Benchmark (one-pager): role_family, role_level, canonical competencies with target scores, salary midpoint, external T2C estimate, recommended interview rubric.
- Evidence packet: last performance rating, 30/60/90 notes, sample PR/feature, training completions, manager assessment (200–400 words).
- Skill Supply Map CSV headers: role_family, role_level, incumbents, pct_at_or_above_target, projected_attrition_6m, open_reqs, recommended_action.

Prioritization rubric (applied in weekly review)

Score each gap 0–10 and compute weighted total:
- Business criticality (40%): Impact on revenue, customer SLAs, or launch commitments.
- Time sensitivity (25%): How quickly gap must be closed to avoid delivery risk.
- Internal readiness (15%): Availability of internal candidates or trainers.
- Hire difficulty (20%): Market scarcity and expected time-to-hire.

Decision thresholds

- Hire: Weighted score >= 7.5 and headcount budget available.
- Upskill: Weighted score between 4.0–7.4 and internal readiness >= 60%.
- Contractor/Interim: Weighted score >= 6.0 and time sensitivity high (T2C < 8 weeks required).

Tooling and automation

- Data extraction: weekly ETL job from Workday/Greenhouse into PDW (owned by Data Platform).
- Survey collection: 1-click manager survey distributed via Slack workflow (People Ops maintains templates).
- Automated dashboard: Skill Supply Map dashboard in Looker (People Ops + Workforce Planning) with filters by team, role level, and recruitment stage.

KPIs and SLAs (program-level)

- Mapping freshness: 100% of in-scope role families updated every quarter; PDW snapshots finished within 10 business days of quarter start.
- Gap closure velocity: 60% of approved gap closure actions closed or in active progress within 90 days.
- Time-to-hire (priority gaps): reduce median TTH from offer to start by 20% within two quarters for gaps scoped as Hire.
- First-90-day time-to-impact: measure via onboarding impact survey; target 70% of new hires meeting role benchmark or above at day 90 for prioritized hires.

Rollout plan (pilot -> broader adoption)

- Q1 pilot: 6 role-families (Engineering infra, Inference runtime, Applied ML, Product, SRE, DevRel). Collect learnings and refine rubric.
- Q2 expansion: add remaining engineering and product families; incorporate feedback loops to Recruiting and L&D.
- Q3+: add non-engineering functions after validating tool flows (HRIS integration, manager training).

Implementation checklist (first quarter)

- [ ] Finalize canonical competencies and rubrics with Discipline Leads. (Owner: People Ops)
- [ ] Wire PDW ETL and Looker dashboard. (Owner: Data Platform)
- [ ] Publish manager survey and manager training (30-minute onboarding session). (Owner: People Ops + L&D)
- [ ] Run pilot for 6 role families. (Owner: Program Owner)
- [ ] Convene prioritization review and record decisions in the Recruiting board. (Owner: Hiring Velocity)

Communication and manager expectations

- Managers must submit evidence packets for direct reports during the evidence gathering window. Missing packets trigger an escalation email to the manager and their director.
- Hiring decisions that exceed base budget require Finance and VP People approval and an updated business case.

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: Manager survey fatigue leading to low-quality evidence.
  - Mitigation: Keep survey < 15 minutes and provide an autopopulated evidence template.
- Risk: Market signals lag leading to mis-prioritization.
  - Mitigation: Recruiting to run a short market check for flagged high-difficulty roles each month.

FAQ

Q: How often will my team be assessed?
A: Every quarter for in-scope families. Ad-hoc updates can be requested before the quarterly run for urgent reorganizations.

Q: Can managers request exceptions to the prioritization outcome?
A: Yes — exceptions are reviewed by the Workforce Planning chair and People Ops; the request must include a 1-page impact memo.
